body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Thursday, October 1, and the day's top story is a shooting call in east Bakersfield that had officers and medics out before dawn, plus a stabbing on Chester Avenue and a pair of semi-truck incidents on Highway 46 and Highway 58. Expect a hot one — a high near 98 — with no weather alerts and one active fire, the Grapevine Fire, still being worked by crews.

## The Kern Overnight

The overnight log opened with a shooting call at 12:25 a.m. in east Bakersfield, where a caller told officers a man stepped out of a white four-door sedan, pointed a gun in the air and fired one round, and that a person was bleeding. A second party was reported to have driven a white four-door to a nearby motel, and units were checking the area through the early hours. Not long before that, at 12:18 a.m., crews were sent to an audible burglary alarm at a home on Millwood Way, near Thornwood Drive and Woodcastle Way, to cover the perimeter and the living room door.

At 1:19 a.m., a person walked into a business on Chester Avenue with a stab wound, and deputies and a fire crew responded to the area around Decatur Street and North Chester Avenue. On the highways, two semis — a maroon rig with a silver trailer and a Walmart semi — collided at 4:33 a.m. in the eastbound lanes of Highway 46 west of Interstate 5 and ended up stuck together in the roadway, forcing a backup and closing an exit while drivers were routed around. Earlier, at 10:39 p.m., a semi was reported on fire in the westbound lanes of Highway 58, and fire crews from a nearby station knocked down a grass fire in the same stretch shortly after. At 5:12 a.m., a silver sedan rolled over near East Brundage Lane and Kincaid Street, drawing a full rescue response; all parties were reported out of the vehicles.

The rest of the log was the usual mix — medical aids on Ponce de Leon Avenue, Primrose Avenue, and at White Lane and Hughes Lane, a vehicle fire north of Panama Road and Cottonwood Road, a shots-fired call on Hall Road near the Rasmussen Center, a robbery alarm at a Dollar General on the 2900 block of Niles Street, and a possible drunken driver reported in a white Mercedes SUV that couldn't hold its speed.

## Today's weather

It's currently 88 degrees at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 98 and a low around 68 tonight. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, but fire crews are on one active fire in the county — the Grapevine Fire — so the dry heat is worth keeping in mind if you're out and about. Air quality readings weren't available this morning. If you've got outdoor plans, the cooler hours are early and late; the middle of the day will feel like the valley in October usually does.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield police are asking for the public's help identifying two men accused of a burglary on Ming Avenue.** The department put out the call to the community as investigators work to identify the pair. If you have information, the department is the place to bring it — this is one where a neighbor who saw something may be exactly what moves the case.

**According to 23ABC, an Oildale woman says she was set on fire at a local homeless encampment in July and that the people she accuses remain free months later.** Frances Lopez, 33, told the station she was visiting a friend's tent on July 11 when three people confronted her friend over a money dispute, and that the encounter turned violent — she says gasoline was thrown and a flame lit, and she escaped the burning tent and made her way to a nearby trailer park for help. She spent nearly eight weeks in a Fresno burn unit, underwent four surgeries, and says doctors found second- and third-degree burns across 32 percent of her body. She's home now but still healing, with open wounds and daily dressing changes, and she told 23ABC she's frustrated that no arrests have been made.

**KGET 17 also reports on substance abuse recovery in Kern County, with the message that addiction "is not because of a moral failure."** The story centers on how recovery works here and the people doing it, framing addiction as a health issue rather than a character flaw. It's a useful read for anyone in Kern who has watched a family member or friend struggle and wondered where to turn.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Bakersfield police have released week-one statistics from the Kern County Fair: three arrests, 28 ejections, and 20 missing-or-found kids.** The numbers give a sense of what a fair week looks like for officers working the grounds — mostly a lot of reuniting kids with their families. It's a reminder, as the fair continues, to keep an eye on little ones in the crowds.

**23ABC reports that a stretch of Highway 46 in San Luis Obispo County has officially been designated the James Dean Memorial Highway, 71 years after the actor's death.** Dean was headed west on Highway 46 on Sept. 30, 1955, and his final drive brought him through Kern County, including a stop at Blackwells Corner, before he continued toward the Central Coast. He was 24 when he died in the crash. Assemblymember Dawn Addis sponsored the resolution naming 4.3 miles of the new alignment, and Caltrans notes the road itself is transformed from the two-lane highway Dean knew into a divided expressway.

**And 23ABC reports that a medical helicopter transporting a patient crashed off Catalina Island on Wednesday night, killing two people, hospitalizing two, and leaving a fifth person missing as of Thursday.** The Coast Guard, area firefighters, and Los Angeles County Sheriff's divers worked through the night, and the search for the missing person continued Thursday morning alongside dives on the wreckage. The FAA said the pilot and a cabin crew member were killed, another cabin crew member was seriously injured, and a passenger had minor injuries. The cause was not immediately clear.

## Something good

The Running with the Angels 5K is returning to Bakersfield, and it's the kind of event that matters quietly. It's a community gathering for families honoring babies lost too soon — a shared morning to remember and to stand with one another. If you've been looking for a way to support neighbors carrying that kind of loss, this is a gentle place to start.

## Coming up this week

The Planning Commission meets tonight, Thursday, October 1, at 5:30 p.m. — the first of a run of public meetings this month. Next week, the City Council holds two sessions on Wednesday, October 7: a 3:30 p.m. meeting and a 5:15 p.m. meeting. The Housing and Community Development Committee meets Thursday, October 8, at noon. If you've got opinions about what's being built or funded around town, these are the rooms where it gets decided.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate ahead. The Cults & Classics season pass for 2026–2027 is on sale now, and the series brings *Young Frankenstein* to the Fox on Monday, October 5. NB RIDAZ takes the stage Friday, October 9, with the Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. United We Dance brings an all-night festival-energy show on Friday, October 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour lands Saturday, October 17.

Have a good Thursday, Bakersfield — stay cool out there, and keep an eye on your neighbors.

top.title: Bakersfield PD asking for public's help identifying 2 men accused of burglary on Ming Ave
